title: Where is Allah? And how does He watch over us?
summary: The correct answer according to the understanding of Ahl al-Sunnah: Allah is above the heavens, exalted above His Throne, above all His creation, and at the same time, He is with us through His knowledge, hearing, and sight—He sees us, hears us, and knows what is in our hearts. In the hadith, the Prophet ﷺ asked a young girl, 'Where is Allah?' and she said, 'In the sky,' and he affirmed her answer. Teach your child that Allah always sees him, even when no one else does—not to frighten him, but to cultivate in him *murāqabah* (watchfulness): that he feels haya (modesty) before his Lord and does good even in secret. This self-watchfulness is the most precious thing you can plant in him, and it will guard him when you are not around.
try_this: This week: When your child does something good and no one sees it, gently remind him, 'Our Lord saw you, and He is happy with you.' And make 'Allah sees me' the motto of your home.
reflection_prompts: How do you balance using 'Allah sees you' as a motivator for good without turning it into constant fear?
What is the difference between a child who behaves well out of fear of punishment and a child who feels haya before his Lord?

review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'في السماء' (in the sky/heaven), but the English renders it as 'above the heavens'. This changes the spatial description and creates inconsistency with the hadith translation later in the text, where the same phrase is correctly translated as 'In the sky'.
